newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said a report on human rights in Turkey would be discussed during Wednesday's Commission meeting but foresaw no decision yet.

In answer to a question, spokesman Filippo di Robilant said there were still problems in controlling overfishing in several member states such as United Kingdom but added that controls were member states' responsibility.
In answer to a question, Josep Coll i Carbo said that a cooperation agreement was under negotiation with Cambodia but that no agreement had been concluded yet.

Asked about Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring's role in the Middle East peace process, Coll i Carbo said it was not to take part in the bilateral negotiations but to try to contribute to a possible solution.
Coll i Carbo also said the Commission was due to join the troika during its visit in the area.
He also said senior government officials from every country taking part in the Euro-Mediterranean partnership launched in Barcelona were meeting in Brussels to decide on follow-up action.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/897: Commission approves the creation of the CLT-UFA joint venture.
- IP/96/900: Commission approves joint venture to provide financing services in the agricultural sector.
- IP/96/901: Commission approves joint venture to supply meter-reading services in Great-Britain.
- IP/96/902: The Commission clears a concentration in the British Railways sector.
- IP/96/904: Palestinians in need: Commission backs humanitarian aid package.
- IP/96/905: Ritt Bjerregaard: We need market quotas for HCFCs in order to safeguard the EU phase-out programme for ozone depleting substances.
- Speech/96/239: Speech by Commissioner Padraig Flynn on U.K. interim measures cases.
- Speech/96/240: Speech by Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy on the state of advancement of preparatory works for euro.
